policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads "an apostle of Christ Jesus"; the English word order renders Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, not the transposed Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
ASV transliterates "Colossae" with omicron in the second syllable, reflecting Κολοσσαῖς rather than Κολασσαῖς.
ASV ends the salutation at "from God our Father" with no "and the Lord Jesus Christ"; the longer reading is unrendered.
ASV reads "to God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ" in apposition; the added καὶ would give "God and Father", which the ASV does not have.
ASV "praying always for you" renders either περὶ or ὑπὲρ with the same English preposition; no ASV note bears on the unit.
ASV "the love which ye have toward all the saints" renders the relative clause ἣν ἔχετε; the bare article τὴν leaves "which ye have" without a source.
ASV "even as it is also in all the world" already carries "also" from the καθὼς καὶ preceding the phrase; a further καὶ after κόσμῳ joining the participles is not separately rendered either way.
ASV reads "even as ye learned of Epaphras" with no adverbial "also"; the added καὶ is unrendered. The verse's textual note concerns our/your, not this unit.
ASV text reads "on our behalf" (ἡμῶν) and the mapped textual note "Many ancient authorities read your" records ὑμῶν as the rejected alternative.
ASV "to walk worthily of the Lord" leaves the infinitive's subject unexpressed, as it would with or without an explicit ὑμᾶς.
ASV "increasing in the knowledge of God", with its note "Or, by", renders a plain dative τῇ ἐπιγνώσει; εἰς τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν would give "unto the knowledge".
ASV text reads "who made us meet" (ἡμᾶς) and the mapped textual note "Some ancient authorities read you" records ὑμᾶς as the rejected alternative.
ASV "all things" is the same English for πάντα and τὰ πάντα; the Greek article is not separately rendered.
ASV renders the substantives without a distinguishing article in English; the presence or absence of τὰ leaves the wording unchanged.
ASV "who is the beginning" supplies the English article for the predicate noun whether or not ἡ stands in the Greek.
ASV renders a second "through him, I say", with "I say" marking the resumed phrase; the repeated δι᾽ αὐτοῦ is present in the text translated.
The verse renders both "things upon the earth" and "things in the heavens", so the English does not show which phrase this preposition stands in or which form it took.
ASV text reads the active "hath he reconciled" (ἀποκατήλλαξεν); the mapped textual note "Some ancient authorities read ye have been reconciled" records the passive ἀποκατηλλάγητε as the alternative.
ASV "in all creation" renders πάσῃ κτίσει the same with or without the article τῇ.
ASV "but now hath it been manifested" renders νῦν and νυνὶ identically; the emphatic form has no separate English.
ASV "which is Christ in you" uses the neuter relative agreeing with "mystery"; the masculine ὅς would give "who".
ASV reads "perfect in Christ" with no "Jesus"; the added Ἰησοῦ is unrendered.
